headline: BOARD RECONCILED TO THE r#13 STATE (lane D13, 2026-08-30) — A RECORDS ACT: no solve, no re-score, no verdict edited, and NO ISO'S GATE OPENS. The top-level prose below had fallen behind this board's own per-ISO blocks; it now says what they already said, plus one signed ruling executed. THREE THINGS. (1) OWNER RULING Q7 — 'MEASURED CLOSES THE LEG' (r#13 sitting, 2026-08-30; docs/handoffs/capx-director-ledger-2026-08.md §0j.3 and §3 Q7). Charter §2.1b(2)(c) requires the crossover input gap (FC-4) MEASURED AND REPORTED — never in-band — so ERCOT, PJM and MISO's leg (c) flips fail → PASS-ON-MEASUREMENT, each on a registered, measured FC-4 and a green readiness battery. THEIR FC-4s ARE ALL FAIL AND STAY QUOTED AT FULL MAGNITUDE (ERCOT price to 68.7% and co2 to 50.6%; PJM co2 to 54.2%; MISO co2 to 75.5%) [D5-R 2026-08-30, owner ruling Q12: those three co2 magnitudes were the PRE-REPAIR crossover scorer's — dominated by a class-grain scoring drop (the model's unsplit-COAL generation read as zero CO2), not dispatch error. On the repaired committed re-measures co2 reads ERCOT −25.2/−23.2/+1.3 %, PJM −7.4/−10.3/−1.1 %, MISO +1.2/−1.8/+13.4 %; NYISO is the exact no-op control and NEISO moved ≤+0.49 pp. Price/volume magnitudes are unaffected, every FC-4 verdict is unchanged, and NO GATE LEG MOVES — a re-scored measurement is still measured (Q7). See `d5r_co2_grain_repair`.]: the leg records that the input gap was MEASURED, and what it measured is large. NYISO's D10 PASS stands. Leg (c) now fails in exactly TWO ISOs — NEISO and CAISO — and in both for one reason only: no T1-X has EVER been run for them. [UPDATED 2026-08-30, lane D14: NEISO's first T1-X is now RUN AND REGISTERED (`neiso-t1x`, FC-4 measured — FAIL at full magnitude, quarantine PASS), so leg (c) now fails ONLY in CAISO.] This is the reading card A-A was signed on, applied without exception, and it supersedes the D7-era in-band reading the board carried simultaneously. (2) NEISO IS THE PROGRAM LEAD, since the S-4V measurement of 2026-08-30: (a) PASS · (b) PASS · (c) PASS on measurement (lane D14, 2026-08-30 — `neiso-t1x`, FC-4 FAIL reported at full magnitude) · (d) none — the FIRST ISO IN PROGRAM HISTORY to hold (a)+(b)+(c); only leg (d), the explicit per-campaign owner authorization, remains. NYISO reads (a) fail (its `complete` marker WITHDRAWN by the r#12 Q5 ruling, executed as Q5-W) · (b) PASS · (c) PASS · (d) none. PJM holds (a) and (c). THREE ISOs now hold exactly two of the four legs, by three DIFFERENT pairs, and NO ISO HOLDS THREE. (3) PJM'S I7 MISS IS RESTATED UPWARD, ON PURPOSE: 366 MW → 5,858 MW (3.39% of gross peak, 2030) under the owner-signed HOLD-LAST-FPR convention (card C-A), with 2029 plausibly joining as a second failing year — an INFERENCE, flagged, which lane S-6 measures. PJM's leg (b) does not move: fail before, fail after. Any reading of PJM's I7 gap as '366 MW' is dead. STILL TRUE, AND STILL THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF: NO ISO CLEARS THE §2.1b FULL-SOLVE AUTHORIZATION GATE. Leg (d) is `none` for all six — there is no standing authorization and none was created here; every ISO's `open` is false and every `closed_on` still names at least one leg. The three legs that moved moved on a signed ruling about what leg (c) MEASURES, not on any improvement in the model. This board is the §2.1b evidence, not a green-wash (rule 1): the program's two non-HOLD T1-F determinations sit behind a withdrawn marker (NYISO) and, for NEISO, a crossover now measured FC-4 FAIL at full magnitude (lane D14 — measured closes the leg, the miss stays reported; leg (d) is untouched), the dominant adequacy blocker still reaches four of six ISOs, and PJM's headline miss just got sixteen times worse because the honest bar is higher.
gate_reading: THE DOMINANT T1-F BLOCKER IS STILL FC-1 ADEQUACY ACCOUNTING, and it now reaches FOUR of six, not five and not all. I7 (accredited firm capacity below the reliability requirement) FAILs in THREE — CAISO, MISO, PJM — and I12 (reserve-margin band) FAILs in TWO, ERCOT and CAISO. TWO ISOs HAVE LEFT THE SET, on measurement in both cases: NYISO's I7 closed 2026-08-25 on a sourced external-capacity intake and its FC-1 is clean 14/14; NEISO's I7 closed 2026-08-30 on the capx-S4 sourced hydro-accreditation factor verified by the S-4V control/treatment pair (I7 PASS 2026-2030), leaving it a LONE I12 WARN which scores CAVEAT, not FAIL. [CORRECTED 2026-08-30 by lane D13: this paragraph read 'it is 5 of 6', 'I7 FAILs in FOUR -- CAISO, MISO, NEISO, PJM' and 'In PJM and NEISO, I7 is the ONLY FC-1 failure left'. All three were stale against this board's own NEISO block from the moment S-4V landed, and S-4V flagged them rather than editing cross-ISO prose outside its charter — see `s4v_neiso_refresh.flagged_not_edited`.] In PJM and MISO, I7 is now the ONLY FC-1 failure left. THE LIVE FC-1 FAIL SETS, exactly: ERCOT {I12, I3} · CAISO {I12, I3, I7} · PJM {I7} · MISO {I7} · NEISO {} (none — lone I12 WARN, CAVEAT) · NYISO {} (none). ON MAGNITUDE, RE-RANKED 2026-08-30 BECAUSE PJM'S BAR MOVED: PJM's I7 miss is no longer the program's smallest. Under the owner-signed hold-last-FPR convention (card C-A; measured by lane S-5) PJM 2030 restates from 366 MW to 5,858 MW (3.39% of gross peak) with 2029 plausibly joining — a flagged inference S-6 measures. The SMALLEST live miss is now MISO 2027 (3,659 MW), with MISO 2026 at 6,037 MW; CAISO remains furthest, failing I7 in four consecutive years (to 9.2 GW) with a 65.5% backstop share — an administrative over-build, not a fleet the screen chose — on top of an I12 band failure and I3 scarcity slack, the same pair ERCOT carries. [CORRECTED 2026-08-30 by lane D13: this passage read 'PJM and NEISO are closest on magnitude (366 MW = 0.24% of requirement, 2030; 218 MW = 0.85%, 2028), though PJM's is UNDERSTATED -- card C's signed convention restates it ... (lane S-5 carries it)'. S-5 has LANDED and the restatement is now on the board, so the understatement is retired rather than forecast; NEISO's 218 MW leg is closed and it is no longer in the set at all.] PROGRAM-WIDE SCORING INSTRUCTION, binding on every lane that reads an I7 miss (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d2b-i7-ledger-2026-08-25.md §7): NO BASE-YEAR I7 LEG IS A CAPACITY-EVOLUTION DEFECT. `evolve_fleet` is SKIPPED when `fleet is None`, so THE BASE YEAR RUNS NO EVOLUTION AT ALL — no adequacy backstop, no retirement screen, no entry. A base-year I7 miss therefore grades INPUT DATA ONLY. MISO 2026 (6,037 MW) and CAISO 2026 (6,577 MW) are base-year legs, and NEITHER BACKSTOP TUNING NOR FLOOR RELAXATION IS EVER THE ANSWER TO ONE — the answers are requirement re-vintage, external-capacity intake and ledger differencing (lanes S-1/S-2/S-3 for MISO; B-1 storage vintage then NQC arming for CAISO). The evolved-year legs (MISO 2027, CAISO 2027-2029, PJM 2030 and now plausibly 2029) add exactly two mechanism-flavoured questions — ladder pacing against real exit waves, which CAISO 2027 answers as working-as-designed, and retirement-screen calibration, PJM's open suspect — and even those sit on top of base ledgers that are provably under-counted (MISO, CAISO). BOTH CLOSURES CAME THIS WAY: NYISO's by a sourced external-capacity intake and NEISO's by a sourced hydro-accreditation factor, neither by tuning. THE §2.1b GATE, SEPARATELY: legs (a)-(d) are conditions on SCHEDULING a full solve, not on model quality, and NO ISO MEETS ALL FOUR. LEG (a) passes for the two `complete` members, NEISO and PJM; NYISO's leg (a) FAILS ON THE MARKER since 2026-08-30 — its `complete` entry was WITHDRAWN by owner ruling (r#12 decision card, Q5: 'Withdraw the marker (CAISO precedent)' — a `complete` marker cannot stand on a NOT-YET keeper, applied uniformly; execution lane Q5-W). LEG (b) passes for TWO, NYISO and NEISO, both PROMOTE-WITH-CAVEATS on their bare t1f keys, and fails for the other four on their HOLD determinations. [CORRECTED 2026-08-30 by lane D13: this read 'Leg (b) now passes for ONE -- NYISO -- and fails for the other five', and, with it, 'NO ISO holds (a) and (b) both'. BOTH ARE FALSE SINCE S-4V: NEISO's bare `neiso-t1f` flipped HOLD -> PROMOTE-WITH-CAVEATS on 2026-08-30 and NEISO holds (a) AND (b). S-4V flagged this rather than editing cross-ISO prose; D13 carries the repair.] LEG (c), AFTER THE OWNER'S Q7 RULING OF 2026-08-30, passes for FOUR — ERCOT, PJM, MISO and NYISO — and FAILS FOR TWO, NEISO and CAISO. The test is the charter's own: FC-4 MEASURED AND REPORTED plus the readiness battery green. The four that pass all have a registered T1-X, and ALL FOUR OF THEIR FC-4s ARE FAIL, quoted at full magnitude in their cells (ERCOT price to 68.7% / co2 to 50.6%; PJM co2 to 54.2%; MISO co2 to 75.5%; NYISO price +29.9%/-24.0%, co2 only 3.9-10.3%) — the crossover input gap is measured and, for three of the four, it is large [D5-R 2026-08-30: the three large co2 magnitudes are the pre-repair instrument's (class-grain drop, repaired — `d5r_co2_grain_repair`); on the repaired committed re-measures the input gap that stays LARGE is price/volume (ERCOT price to 68.7 %), while co2 reads −25.2/−23.2/+1.3 (ERCOT), −7.4/−10.3/−1.1 (PJM), +1.2/−1.8/+13.4 (MISO) %. No leg moves]. The two that fail have never run a T1-X at all: no `neiso-t1x` or `caiso-t1x` key exists and FC-4 reads n/a. [CORRECTED 2026-08-30 by lane D13: this read 'LEG (c) NOW FAILS FOR ALL SIX ISOs', which was superseded first by lane D10's measured NYISO PASS (2026-08-30) and then by ruling Q7. The board had been carrying BOTH readings at once — the very defect Q7 was raised to settle.] LEG (d) is 'none' everywhere — there is NO standing authorization, and no ISO's gate opened from this refresh or any before it. WHERE THAT LEAVES THE SIX, LEG COUNT ONLY: NEISO (a)+(b) · NYISO (b)+(c) · PJM (a)+(c) · ERCOT (c) · MISO (c) · CAISO none. Three ISOs hold two legs by three different pairs; nobody holds three; leg (d) is held by nobody and is granted per campaign, never standing. The single chartered lane that could produce a first three-leg ISO is D14 (a NEISO T1-X), which would close NEISO's (c) on measurement exactly as D10 closed NYISO's. WHAT THIS READING IS NOT: it is not a re-score. Every verdict quoted here already existed in a committed record before the session that wrote it; this board only stops describing superseded ones, and applies signed dispositions. THE 2026-08-30 D13 EDIT IS LIKEWISE NOT A RE-SCORE: three gate legs moved (ERCOT/PJM/MISO (c) fail -> pass) on an owner ruling about what leg (c) measures, and one magnitude was restated (PJM I7, on a landed FINDING); every verdict on this board keeps its own scoring provenance, no `fc` scorecard entry changed, and no ISO's schedulability changed in either direction.
